explanation: Precompute which substrings are palindromes using matching endpoints and their inner substring. Then backtrack over every palindromic next piece, preserving text order. Copy each completed partition, including the empty partition for empty text.
timeComplexity: O(n²+n·2ⁿ) worst case, including output construction At most 2^(n-1) cut subsets exist; recording a partition requires its pieces. The table variants additionally fill n² cells.
spaceComplexity: O(n²+n) auxiliary, plus output Palindrome tables use n² flags in table variants; path, copied prefixes and output costs are counted separately.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract.
correctness: The table marks a substring palindromic exactly when its endpoints match and its interior is palindromic, with one- and two-character base cases. Backtracking chooses only such substrings and tries every next boundary, so it enumerates precisely all palindrome partitions.
walkthrough: For pop, choosing single characters produces [p,o,p]. The entire substring pop is also palindromic, producing [pop]. No other next boundary yields a palindrome partition.
edgeCases: An empty string has one empty partition.
Repeated characters can create exponentially many valid partitions.
Character positions in this implementation are UTF-16 code units, not user-perceived grapheme clusters.
